R0001.title: Process Automation
R0001.definition: Includes but is not limited to automated registration, login, shopping, coupon collection, lottery, and task completion — using unintended application operations to accelerate or schedule specific workflows.
R0001.description: There are two mainstream approaches to implementing process automation: one is to reverse-engineer the business workflow and data transmission protocol, then write automated scripts to send requests; the other is to manipulate the business access terminal (e.g., browser, mobile app) and replay pre-recorded workflow actions. The former corresponds to protocol-level automation (R0001-001) and the latter to automated simulators (R0001-002).
R0001.influence: Exploits platform promotional benefits and occupies resources intended for legitimate users.

observables: A single account issues high-frequency requests across multiple marketing endpoints within a short window
Request timing across registration/login/coupon/task endpoints is highly regular with minimal interval variance
A single device fingerprint or IP is tied to many accounts running the same task sequence concurrently
Newly registered accounts complete the full coupon-collection to order to withdrawal chain within an extremely short time

R0001-001.title: Protocol-Level Automation
R0001-001.definition: Refers to programs that bypass the front-end interface and directly send network protocol requests to execute business workflows.
R0001-001.description: Attackers reverse-engineer the business workflow and data transmission protocol, then write automated scripts that send requests directly to backend APIs, completing registration, login, coupon-claim, ordering, and other flows without front-end interaction. This approach is highly efficient and scales to large concurrent volumes, and is commonly used for promo abuse, flash-sale grabbing, and metric inflation. Because requests lack browser event chains and human-interaction traces, they are hard to block with conventional front-end checks.
R0001-001.influence: Exploits platform promotional benefits and occupies resources intended for legitimate users.

observables: Request timing across marketing endpoints is highly regular, with minimal variance in inter-request intervals
Requests lack front-end interaction telemetry and browser event chains, hitting backend protocols directly
The same IP or device fingerprint carries multiple account tokens to concurrently call coupon-claim and order endpoints within a short window
Request headers show highly homogeneous UA, Referer, and device parameters, or are missing browser fingerprint fields

R0001-002.title: Automated Simulator
R0001-002.definition: Refers to simulator programs that mimic normal user behavior to automatically send network protocol requests.
R0001-002.description: By manipulating the business access terminal (e.g., browser, mobile app), pre-recorded workflow actions are replayed repeatedly. Using simulators, device-control systems, or UI automation tools, attackers mimic genuine clicks, swipes, and inputs to bypass protocol-level detection, suiting scenarios with human-verification challenges. The approach preserves front-end event chains but exhibits mechanical timing and regular trajectories, and is commonly used for bulk account farming, promotional activity cheating, and flash-sale grabbing.
R0001-002.influence: Exploits platform promotional benefits and occupies resources intended for legitimate users.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-020 Account Aggregation

observables: Mouse trajectories and click coordinates show straight-line or equidistant patterns, lacking human jitter and acceleration/deceleration curves
Page dwell time is highly consistent, with fixed and repeatable intervals between each action step
The same device fingerprint cluster concurrently executes identical recorded script action sequences
Touch-event pressure, tilt angle, and other sensor data are missing or stuck at constant values

R0001-003.title: Automated Login Risk
R0001-003.definition: The identity authentication login process can be automated, creating security risks.
R0001-003.description: Automated login risk refers to the use of automated scripts, bots, or software to execute the login process. Attackers use automation to fire login requests in bulk, often combined with credential stuffing, password brute-forcing, and CAPTCHA recognition to break authentication, which then provides an identity foundation for downstream abuse such as account farming, promo abuse, and account aggregation. It also amplifies the threat surface of credential cracking and credential stuffing, and is a typical manifestation of process automation in the login stage.
R0001-003.influence: Can lead to credential cracking (R0032), credential stuffing (R0032-001), and other cyberattacks; can also be used for automated account seasoning (R0034) and third-party account aggregation (R0037), making it a priority defense target.

observables: The same account fires login requests from multiple IPs/devices within a short window
Login endpoint frequency spikes, with password field hash values highly concentrated
Immediately after login, the session jumps to high-value actions (coupon claim, order) with no normal browsing trail
